newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures firm on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures firm on short-covering.

text.p: The UK wheat futures market saw prices end 0.50 to 0.75 up on short-covering, market sources said on Wednesday. The January contract traded up 0.50 stg to reach an intraday high of 96.25 stg per tonne and March found an extra 0.75 to trade at 95.25.

"There has also been a bit of spreading, there's evidence that consumers are still sniffing about but it does seem that farmers have done a lot of clearing out already and gone quiet perhaps until after Christmas," one trader said. "It's hard to find a reason for the market to turn bullish so it's all a bit one-sided at the moment," another said.
Turnover reached 371 lots by the close.
The November wheat futures contract lost 0.15 points on nearing expiry with just 52 lots traded.
Barley futures were unchanged with the exception of the November contract which traded 0.50 stg per tonne down at 92.50 before fade-out on Friday.
Traders expect the market to remain quiet into next week on limited farm activity.
The Amsterdam milling wheat futures contract was unchanged with one lot traded.
Market sources attributed the lack of active business in physical grains to pre-Christmas lethargy.
"It's basically due to limited offers from farmers and the fact that exporters simply aren't selling," one said.
Prices were 0.50 to 1.00 stg per tonne up on short-covering.
November milling wheat 11 percent protein was up 0.50 stg per tonne at 155.50.
Norfolk/Suffolk feedwheat for November delivery traded at around 97.00 stg.
